start.title: Your bins
start.description:
How should Bins Out know your collection days?

**From my council (recommended):** your dates stay up to date by themselves, including bank holiday changes. This needs **Waste Collection Schedule**, a free integration you install from HACS, with your council and address added to it. Bins Out shows you how if it isn't set up yet.

**Myself:** enter one collection date for each bin and how many weeks apart collections are. Nothing else to install.

menu_options.council: From my council (needs Waste Collection Schedule)

council_pick.title: Your council
council_pick.description:
Pick your council from the councils you've added to Waste Collection Schedule.

**Can't see your council?** This list only shows councils already added there. [Add my council]({add_council_url}), then come back to Bins Out → Configure → Add bins from my council.

council_install.title: Your council
council_install.description:
Bins Out gets your council's dates from **Waste Collection Schedule**, a free add-on that supports hundreds of councils. It isn't installed yet.

1. [Open Waste Collection Schedule in HACS]({hacs_url}), download it, and restart Home Assistant.
2. Add your council and address there. Many UK councils ask for your UPRN: [find yours]({uprn_url}).
3. Come back here and choose **I've added my council**.

council_add.title: Your council
council_add.description:
You haven't added a council to Waste Collection Schedule yet.

1. [Add my council]({add_council_url}): choose your country, search for your council, and enter your address. Many UK councils ask for your UPRN: [find yours]({uprn_url}).
2. Come back here and choose **I've added my council**.

council_bins.title: Your collections
council_bins.description: These collections are on {calendar}. Tick the ones you have; each becomes a bin. Names and colours are a best guess: change them afterwards with Configure, Edit a bin.

bin.title: Bin
bin.description: Name it, pick its colour and what kind of container it is, and choose where its collection dates come from.

data_description.repeat_weeks: Some councils only publish the next date. Bins Out uses this to show the weeks after it as estimates. Leave at 0 to let Bins Out work it out from the council's dates. Council dates always come first.
data_description.container: Used for its picture on the dashboard and what Alexa calls it. Leave blank to guess from the name ("Food" is a caddy).

bin_manual.title: {name}: collection dates
bin_manual.description: Pick any date this bin was or will be collected. Every other date is worked out from it.

alexa.title: Alexa announcements
alexa.description:
Have Alexa say your reminders out loud, e.g. "put the grey recycling bin out tonight". On an Echo Show the words also appear on the screen.

This needs **Alexa Media Player**, a free integration: [get it from HACS]({alexa_hacs_url}), restart Home Assistant, then add it in Settings → Devices & services and sign in to Amazon. Your Echo devices then appear in the list below.

data.alexa_test: Send a test announcement when I save

data_description.alexa_test: Alexa says "This is Bins Out. Your bin reminders will be announced here." so you can check it works.

alexa_tested.title: Did Alexa say it?
alexa_tested.description:
Your Echo devices should have said "This is Bins Out. Your bin reminders will be announced here."

Nothing? Check the Echo isn't on Do Not Disturb, try **Just speak** instead of **Announce**, and check Alexa Media Player is signed in (Settings → Devices & services).

messages.title: Reminder messages
messages.description:
Choose what the reminders say, on Alexa and in notifications.

**{bins}** is replaced by the bins' names, e.g. *the blue bin and the grey food caddy*. **{was}** becomes *was* or *were* to match. Clear a box to go back to the standard wording.

data.message_try: Say the evening message on Alexa when I save

data_description.message_try: Alexa says it with your own bins' names, so you can hear how it sounds.

phones.title: Phone notifications
phones.description:
Have the reminders pop up on your phone and vibrate, asking **Have you put it out?** Tap **Yes** to tell Bins Out it's out, or **Not yet** to be asked again an hour later (until 22:00 the night before, or until collection time in the morning). Tap the notification to open the Bins page.

This needs the free **Home Assistant app** on each phone, signed in to this Home Assistant: [get the app]({app_url}). Phones with the app then appear in the list below.

data.phone_home_only: Only phones that are at home
data.phone_test: Send a test notification when I save

data_description.phone_home_only: Phones that are away from home are skipped. If nobody's home, every phone is reminded. Uses the phone's location from the Home Assistant app.
data_description.phone_test: Your phones get "This is Bins Out. Your bin reminders will pop up here." so you can check it works.

phones_tested.title: Did it pop up?
phones_tested.description:
Your phones should have buzzed with "This is Bins Out. Your bin reminders will pop up here."

Nothing? On the phone:
- **Settings → Apps → Home Assistant → Notifications**: allowed.
- **Settings → Apps → Home Assistant → Battery**: Unrestricted (Android), so the app isn't asleep.
- In the Home Assistant app, **Settings → Companion app → Notification history** shows whether it arrived.
- On an iPhone, allow notifications for Home Assistant in Settings → Notifications.

calendar_missing.title: Bins Out can't find your council calendar
calendar_missing.description:
The council calendar {calendar} has gone, so these bins can't get new collection dates: {bins}. Until it's fixed they keep their last known dates, which will soon run out.

This usually means your council was removed from Waste Collection Schedule. To fix it, either:

- add your council to Waste Collection Schedule again (Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Waste Collection Schedule), then open Bins Out → Configure → Edit a bin and pick the new calendar for each bin; or
- remove those bins in Bins Out → Configure → Remove a bin.

This notice goes away by itself once the bins have a calendar again.
